sanskrit_verse: स्वकामे वर्तमाना तु या स्नेहान् न निवारिता । अवश्या सा भवेत् पश्चाद् यथा व्याधिरुपेक्षिता ॥
transliteration: svakāme vartamānā tu yā snehān na nivāritā | avaśyā sā bhavet paścād yathā vyādhir upekṣitā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: She who remains indulgent in her own desire, unrestrained by affectionate bonds, shall inevitably fall into degradation—just as a disease ignored becomes severe.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from alignment with cosmic order, not personal will
Causation flows from neglect of dharma-leading to natural consequence
Capacity-based responsibility requires conscious regulation of desire
Restoration logic demands early intervention before imbalance deepens
Consciousness alignment prevents the collapse into self-destructive patterns
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual acts solely on personal desire without dharmic restraint THEN automatic restoration protocol initiates through community guidance structures
IF emotional bonds fail to regulate harmful self-indulgence THEN capacity-building interventions are mandatorily deployed
IF early signs of deviation appear AND no internal correction occurs THEN external realignment mechanisms activate
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that unregulated personal autonomy leading to societal harm invokes mandatory restorative review rather than punitive measures. The threshold of responsibility lies in the failure to self-regulate when supported by relational and social structures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that unchecked desire leads to inevitable downfall—anupūrvaśaḥ demonstrates how neglect at subtle levels manifests gross consequences. Proportional responsibility lies not in blame but in restoring balance through guided introspection and systemic support. Non-punitive reality affirms that suffering emerges naturally from misalignment; thus, justice intervenes to prevent further entropy of consciousness.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate guided self-reflection programs under qualified mentors
Deploy peer accountability circles to restore relational harmony
Activate karmic completion processes through structured service engagement
Reintegrate individual into dharmic community framework via ritual affirmation
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Desire unbound leads to decay; therefore, consciousness must be realigned through dharmic restoration—not punishment. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate judge.
